 THESE APPEALS ARE FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 01.01.2018 PASSED IN MVC NOS. 773/2016 AND 772/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND XIII ADDITIONAL MACT, SORABA, ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In these appeals, the petitioners have challenged the common judgment and award dated 01.01.2018 passed in M.V.C.Nos.772/2016 and 773/2016 by the court of the Senior Civil Judge and XIII AMACT-Court, Soraba ('the Tribunal' for short).

sentences.text: 2 2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Briefly stated the facts are, on 11.08.2015 at about 9.30 a.m., A.P.Dadasab (petitioner in MVC No.772/2016) while riding the motor bike bearing No.KA-15/5520 along with Kumari Athiyar Rabbiya (petitioner in MVC No.773/2016) as pillion rider, near Ankaravalli village bus stand, a Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-31/9181 hit against them injuring both.
After taking treatment at Government Hospital, Soraba, Yenepoya Hospital, Mangalore, both the petitioners have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company of Balero Pickup vehicle.

entities.text: Insurance Company of Balero Pickup vehicle
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Tribunal after taking the evidence on record by impugned judgment, awarded compensation of Rs.1,68,816/- and Rs.1,51,687/- respectively.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of NC: 2023:KHC:41343 compensation
, the petitioners have filed these appeals on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.G.S.Chidambara, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Sharanappa Gowda Malipatil, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place in the year 2015.
Petitioner (Dadasab) suffered Type III B fracture of right leg, the percentage of disability taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side, the income assessed at Rs.4,500/- is very less.

Petitioners have travelled to Mangalore for treatment, huge money was spent towards travelling expenses,
lesser compensation is awarded and sought for enhancement.

It is further contended that the minor petitioner (Kumari Athiyar Rabbiya) was under hospitalization for 26 days, she too sustained fracture of middle third shaft of right leg, NC: 2023:KHC:41343 the award of compensation is on lower side and sought for enhancement.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that after treatment,
fractures have been re-united, there is no abnormality causing the disability, one of the petitioners is 63 years and another is minor 8 years old; there is no question of loss of future earning and the compensation is proportionately awarded by the Tribunal, which does not call for interference and he supported the impugned judgment.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The material on record did point out that there was an accident between the motor cycle and the jeep in which both the petitioners have sustained injuries.
The medical records did point out that the NC: 2023:KHC:41343 petitioner (Dadasab) sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and the minor petitioner suffered fracture of right middle shaft.

Both were under hospitalization, traveled to Mangalore for treatment and they have spent money towards attendant, travelling, food and nourishment, treatment, underwent ordeal of pain and suffering, suffered loss of amenities and discomfort for which they are required to be compensated.

Having regard to the nature of injury sustained by the petitioners, it appears that the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is inadequate NC: 2023:KHC:41343 and the Tribunal did not consider the compensation under the loss of amenities and discomfort, food and nourishment,
loss of income due to laid-up.
Hence, compensation has to be calculated.

11. As regards petitioner (Dadasab), it is proper to assess Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering;
Rs.1,00,336/- was spent by him towards treatment, that has to be reimbursed; loss of amenities and discomfort is assessed at Rs.40,000/-; food and nourishment at Rs.10,000/-; transportation at Rs.8,200/-.
In the year 2015, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.9,000/-.
Keeping that in mind, attendant charges for 41 days at Rs.12,300/- is assessed.
Dr.Shailesh/CW-1 has spoken to about the treatment taken and also injury affecting the earning capacity of the petitioner.
For the age of 63, applicable multiplier is '7'.
If the medical evidence is taken into consideration, loss of disability assessed at 12% is reasonable, but the NC: 2023:KHC:41343 Tribunal has assessed at 8% without any reason.
At the age of 63 years, a person suffering fracture of both bones of right leg will suffer disability not less than 12%.

Hence, taking the said disability,
loss of earning will be : Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 7 x 12% = Rs.90,720/-.
At the age of 63, petitioner requires minimum six months of laid up as he was under hospitalization for 41 days.
Hence, loss of income during laid-up period is assessed at Rs.54,000/-.

The Petitioner is to be compensated as under:

As regards minor injured is concerned,
Having regard to the nature of injuries, the parent had to attend the child for a period of minimum of three months, as she was inpatient for 26 days.
Hence, Rs.27,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during laid-up for one of her parents.

Insofar as loss of future income is concerned, since she was minor aged 8 years, as regards disability is concerned, CW-1/Dr.Shailesh has assessed 5% disability to this petitioner, but the Tribunal took it as 2% and a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is assessed as the compensation towards disability by rightly relying upon the judgment of this Court in Master Mallikarjun -vs- Divisional Manager, the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41343 National Insurance Co.ltd. and Another1
